result.summary:
Lane CB is done for items (1), (2) and (4). Item (3) is done as measurement plus a calibration path; the calibration itself belongs to A-38 and M7.14. All work is in prototypes/m7-sprint1 and docs/m7-plan. Nothing in Sim.Core, Sim.Data, Sim.Cli, Sim.Tests, Sim.Ui, scripts or CI changed, and no unit data or cap value changed.

(1) One rule now serves lanes W and D: `DirectorCaps.EntitiesOf`.
- Soldier classes: min(persons, cap) battle entities. A soldier formation is never refused for size; its persons are limited by the economy.
- Machine classes: one entity per machine, ⌈P/crew⌉, refused above the cap (READING CB-1 (a)). The mortar's crewed tube is kept.
- Uncapped classes: one entity per person (lane N's CAP-5 treatment, kept).
- The rule is used by CountOf/Check, FormationRoster (ReinforceToCaps now fills machine classes only) and both sandbox paths: Quick Battle force creation (one formation per force; the split at the persons cap is removed) and the Campaign Encounter, both through `SandboxSession.Fielded`.
- `FormationSpec.Persons` carries the persons behind the entities. `EntityShare` validates it in both resolvers, and lane MOR's "fight it won" rise now weighs persons in both resolvers.
- 18 lane D test cases moved, each with a measured failure and its attribution written in the test. Re-based sandbox sessions reproduce the base battles' result hashes, measured on 0d2db74. No resolver golden or battery pin moved. There are 18 new test cases.

(2) docs/m7-plan/battle-entity-proposal.md (PROPOSAL) covers:
- the share P/n, made into integers once at the collapse by the largest remainder (Law 1 exact, MEASURED);
- options E1, E2 and E3 for hit points and output (E1 recommended, not built). The MEASURED gap today: an entity fights as one person, so 1,000 v 1,000 is the battle of 50 v 50;
- the AutoResolver in persons;
- morale: the settlement is unchanged, and one in-battle term now counts persons;
- consequences with every data row cited and none changed: CAP-1 and CAP-2 dissolve, no retune is needed;
- MEASURED performance: under DA5, 17.8-22.8 ms per pulse whatever the persons; under the old persons rule, up to 20,332 ms per pulse at 4,000 entities.
- The caps and sandbox proposals are marked "(D-082 DA5)" in place, quoting the text each change replaces.

(3) economic-scale-proposal.md now records DA3 and has a new §8.
- Full research twins at turn 100, six seeds: 10,360-14,380 soldiers accepted at once.
- Capped twins at turns 325 and 400, six seeds: every order accepted, 52,800 and 240,000 soldiers.
- Late stages, turns 500-1630, six seeds: the shipped support test refuses every recruitment at 29 of 30 points, because the purse holds no grain.
- The DERIVED per-soldier cost path grows about a hundredfold from turn 200 to turn 1630.
- The proposed levers: L3 per-identity maintenance, L1 reading all food goods, L4 as an early brake, L6 as the campaign limit.
- The food ordering was not chosen. Both orderings are reported where a result depends on them.

(4) The lane report is H-CB.md.

No reinforcement policy is designed for soldier formations, whose persons are uncapped. ReinforceToCaps serves machine classes only.
Full recruitment twin at turns 325 and 400: NOT RUN (cubic Sim.Core cost, 44 hours to 247 days per twin, extrapolated). Capped twins are lower bounds.
No twin at turn 1630, the campaign's last turn. The latest twin is at turn 1629.
Lane F's food-ordering comparison on research-driven worlds: NOT RUN (its fixtures are order-less). Deferred to A-38 with a research-fixture generator.
The DA3 calibration itself (L3 per-identity maintenance, the L1 support-test change): A-38 and M7.14, after Q3. Only the path and the measurements exist.
Why the purse holds no grain at late stages was not isolated. Lane D's inference stands: the food baskets consume the grain stock.
Late stages are sampled at only five turns per seed; no denser sampling outside lane D's seed 42.
The scale-probe --twin-at option is not checked against the last turn, so a twin there crashes the run (observation, not changed).
open_questions: E1 for M7.6 (battle-entity-proposal.md §3, §8 item 1): should an entity that stands for many persons fight as a proportional block of them (E1, recommended), as a weighted exchange (E2), or stay a representative sample as today (E3)? READING CB-1: is a machine-class entity one machine, with persons limited to cap × crew ((a), applied)? Or do machine entities aggregate like soldier entities ((b))?

CAP-5 performance: uncapped families keep one entity per person. Their tactical cost grows with the square of the entities (MEASURED), and generated-id formations stop at 1,000 entities. Do they get a performance cap (a value only the Director can set), or do they aggregate like soldier classes?
proposals_for_director: Adopt E1, the proportional block, as the M7.6 battle-entity design. At P ≤ cap it is today's engine exactly (INFERRED by construction), and only battles with P > cap would move. Geometry choice and AutoResolver re-fit in persons are in battle-entity-proposal.md §3.3-3.4.

findings.claim: Under DA5 any soldier force is one formation, so SandboxSession.AddForce now reaches the mint transfer at any size. A force larger than the mint's free balance (MintOpening = 10^12, or two forces whose sum exceeds it) makes AddForce throw InvalidOperationException('overdraft'). It throws only after NewFormation has opened a ledger account and used up a formation id, and no log row is written. Afterwards the session hash differs from a fresh session's, the next formation gets id 2 instead of 1, and Replay(session) no longer reproduces the session hash. This breaks the sandbox invariant that only logged edits reach the session (lane D rounds D-R1-10, D-R2-06). Before DA5, the same soldier request was refused (OutOfGrid) or threw in SplitSizes ('too many formations') before anything changed. The before-DA5 behaviour is INFERRED from 0d2db74's AddForce and SplitSizes code; it was not run there. Uncapped gun crews already had this defect before lane CB (MEASURED).
findings.evidence: MEASURED with a temporary probe test in my clone at f454bec (removed afterwards); output in scratchpad m7c/verify-CB-r1/overdraft/probe.txt: 'heavy infantry, MintOpening + 1 persons: InvalidOperationException: overdraft'; 'log rows 0; ledger accounts 5 -> 6; formations 0'; 'session hash equals a fresh session's: False'; 'next AddForce gets formation id 2 (fresh session: 1)'; 'Replay(session) hash equals the session's: False'; 'two forces of 6e11: first None; second: InvalidOperationException: overdraft; log rows 1'; 'uncapped gun crews, MintOpening + 1 (the pre-DA5 path too): InvalidOperationException: overdraft'. Code path: AddForce -> NewFormation: `_ledger.Open(...)`, then `_ledger.Transfer(_mint, acc, persons)` (WarLedger throws 'overdraft'); `_nextId++` happens before that.

findings.claim: The inferred cost of a full recruitment twin, '44–69 hours at turn 325 and 173–247 days at turn 400, per twin', is computed from lane D's four seeds (42, 1, 2, 7) only. Yet it appears in sections built on the lane's six seeds: economic-scale-proposal §8.2.1 lines 278 and 293, H-CB §4 lines 162–163 and §6, and the lane's summary and not_done ('44 hours to 247 days'). The lane's own M3 probe, which I reproduced byte for byte, gives seeds 3 and 5 much lower formula bounds. The same cubic fit then yields 13.6–69.4 hours at turn 325 and 43.2–247.0 days at turn 400 across the six seeds. Line 278 likewise quotes 'lane D's formula bound 1,966,000–2,289,080 and 8,957,200–10,078,380' in a six-seed paragraph; the six-seed bounds are 1,330,040–2,289,080 and 5,638,120–10,078,380. The conclusion (the full twin is not feasible) stands; the stated ranges are mis-scoped.

At turn 400: 8,957,200; 10,078,380; 9,965,360; 9,446,440; 5,638,120; 6,590,800. DERIVED with the lane's own fit, T = 51.1 s x (orders / 6,742)^3 with orders = bound / 20: turn 325, seed 3 66,502 orders = 13.6 h and seed 5 75,916 = 20.3 h; turn 400, seed 3 281,906 = 43.2 days and seed 5 329,540 = 69.1 days. Seeds 42 and 1 give exactly the lane's endpoints (44.0 h / 69.4 h; 173.4 d / 247.0 d).

findings.claim: The 'MEASURED' morale-weight example '10 entities standing for 40 persons -> 88' is a configuration the applied rule never produces. It appears in the battle-entity proposal §4 table (line 182), in H-CB §2.3 and §6 ('MEASURED (33, 88, 0)') and in test case TheFightItWon_…(1UL, 50L, 40L, 88L). Under the applied READING CB-2 (a), a heavy-infantry formation of 40 persons fights as EntitiesOf(HeavyInfantry, 40) = 40 entities, not 10; persons differ from entities only above the cap. The resolvers accept the pair because EntityShare.Validate checks only P >= n (and the land domain), never n = EntitiesOf(class, P). So the 'one rule' holds at the roster and sandbox fielding paths, but not at the shared battle boundary that lane W's M7.15 hand-off will use. The test's reachable cases (persons null -> 33, and 5,000 persons -> 0) still kill the lane's E1–E3 mutants, so the gap is in the claim and the documentation, not in the kill record.
findings.evidence: Code: DirectorCaps.EntitiesOf returns `Math.Min(persons, CapOf(f))` for soldier classes (DirectorCaps.cs:169). EntityShare.Validate (EntityShare.cs) throws only for `s.Domain != Domain.Land` or `p < s.Count`. BattleEntityRuleTests.cs:274 has `[InlineData(1UL, 50L, 40L, 88L)]`, where formation G has Count 10 and Persons 40. battle-entity-proposal.md:182: 'the beaten 10 entities standing for 40 persons → 88'.
